problem: The phrase "stays and can even grow if it is time-locked" is misleading. In the average a time-locked artefact keeps exactly its original amplitude; it does not grow. Only its size relative to the shrinking random noise increases. A student can misread this as "averaging amplifies artefacts".
fix: Averaging reduces random noise, not fixed artefacts. A time-locked 50 Hz hum or an eye blink keeps its full amplitude in the average while the random noise falls by √N, so the artefact looks relatively larger. Remove it with a notch filter, shielding, or trial rejection.
